title: Compact generators and finite-Tor constructible compactness on finite-type etale sites without separatedness
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. No separatedness of $T$ over $k$ is assumed. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and standard cohomology [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Call $E$ bounded constructible if $H^i(E)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$ and each $H^i(E)$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Say $E$ has finite Tor amplitude if there are integers $r\le s$ such that for every sheaf $N$ of $C$-modules placed in degree zero, $H^i(E\otimes_C^L N)=0$ for every $i\notin[r,s]$.

Every bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. There exist a set $S$ in the indexing universe and a family $(E_s)_{s\in S}$ of bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude such that, for every morphism $h:A\to B$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, if postcomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_s[n],B)$ is bijective for all $s\in S$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $h$ is an isomorphism. The category has arbitrary set-indexed coproducts and is locally small in the corresponding Hom universe.

source.place: Section 6.4, hypothesis preceding Example 6.4.1; Example 6.4.1; Lemmas 6.4.2 and 6.4.5; Proposition 6.4.8 (printed pp. 48–49). Bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes agree with the perfect-value constructible complexes of Definition 6.3.1 by Lemma 6.3.7 (printed pp. 45–46) and the finite-Tor perfectness criterion. The section assumes qcqs, not separatedness; finite-type schemes here are Noetherian and qcqs.
